mainTopic: Which rulings of רבי שמעון שזורי are the הלכה: the wooden chest, wine as always תחילה, and his ברייתא about טבל mixed with חולין.
overview: Earlier, רבי חנינא said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, and the גמרא wants to know which case he meant. The first answer points to a משנה about how to measure the size of a wooden chest. רב נחמן בר יצחק points instead to a משנה about liquids that are always תחילה. In that משנה the גמרא fixes the wording so that רבי שמעון שזורי simply says 'wine.' Next comes a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון שזורי's טבל got mixed into חולין, and רבי טרפון told him to separate מעשר from market produce. The גמרא explains that this works because both are exempt by Torah law. A second version says he was told to take from a גוי, and each version explains why the other source would not work. Finally רב פפא rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי even in this ברייתא case. רבי חנינא מסורא then asks why that was not obvious, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: First answer: the case of the wooden chest
steps.stepSummary: The ruling that follows רבי שמעון שזורי is about measuring a chest. The גמרא quotes the משנה where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue over how the chest is measured.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said about a chest, as we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say it is measured from the inside, and בית הלל say from the outside. Both agree that the thickness of the legs and the thickness of the rims is not measured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question of which case רבי חנינא meant: it was the case of a wooden chest. It starts quoting the משנה that sets up the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large wooden chest (big enough to hold 40 סאה) does not become טמא, so its exact size matters. בית שמאי measure only the inside space, while בית הלל also count the walls. Both agree that the legs and rims are not counted.

keyTerms.meaning: A large wooden chest or box
Measured from the inside (only the inner space counts)
From the outside (the walls are counted too)
Thickness or volume
Rims or raised edges around the chest

phrases.english: About a chest, as we learned:
phrases.notes: This answers the earlier question of which case רבי חנינא was ruling on.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say it is measured from the inside,
and Beit Hillel say from the outside,
and both of them agree
that the thickness of the legs
and the thickness of the rims is not measured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section: which ruling of רבי שמעון שזורי did רבי חנינא mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling is about measuring a wooden chest.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of רבי שמעון שזורי's rulings is the הלכה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the legs and rims are measured
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the agreement goes the other way: the legs and rims are counted, but the space between them is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: They agree that the thickness of the legs and rims is measured, but the space between them is not measured.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with רבי יוסי, who disagrees about what בית שמאי and בית הלל agreed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, the solid parts (legs and rims) are added to the measurement. The empty space between the legs is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree
The space between them (between the legs)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: They agree
that the thickness of the legs and the thickness of the rims is measured,
but the space between them is not measured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion in the same משנה, arguing about what was agreed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The legs and rims are measured; the space between them is not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי: it depends on the height of the legs
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי says that if the legs are a טפח high, the space between them is not counted. If they are shorter, it is counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: If the legs were a טפח high, the space between them is not measured. If not, the space between them is measured.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי שמעון שזורי's opinion. According to this answer, this is the opinion רבי חנינא ruled like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A space of a טפח counts as its own separate area, so it is not part of the chest. A smaller space is treated as part of the chest and is included in the measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a basic unit of measure
High, tall
And if not

steps.whatToRemember: By the first answer, רבי חנינא's ruling is that the space between a chest's legs counts toward its size only if the legs are less than a טפח high.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
If the legs were a handbreadth high,
the space between them is not measured,
and if not, the space between them is measured.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיוּ רַגְלַיִם גְּבוֹהוֹת טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion in the משנה, the one the first answer says is the הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The space between the legs counts only if the legs are less than a טפח high.

steps.title: Second answer: רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is about wine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says רבי חנינא's ruling was about wine, and quotes a משנה about liquids that are always תחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It was about wine, as we learned: רבי מאיר says oil is always תחילה. The חכמים say honey too. רבי שמעון שזורי says wine too.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives another answer to which case רבי חנינא meant. He points to a משנה about the טומאה of liquids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A liquid that becomes טמא is always considered תחילה, a first-level טומאה, even when it touched something with a lower level of טומאה. The משנה argues over which liquids belong in this group. רבי שמעון שזורי's opinion on wine is the one that would be the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: First-level טומאה
Always
Oil
Honey
Wine

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַיַּיִן,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: About wine,
as we learned: Rabbi Meir says:
Oil is always first-level,
and the Rabbis say: Honey too,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אַף הַיָּיִן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says: Wine too.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַיַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from the chest case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling is about wine being always תחילה.

steps.title: Does the first תנא think wine is left out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording 'wine too.' Does that imply the earlier opinion holds wine is not included?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean the first תנא holds that wine is not included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem with the wording of the משנה it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'wine too' suggests wine is an extra item that the others do not accept. But it is hard to think that the earlier opinion would leave out wine, the most obvious liquid of all.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from this we would learn
The first opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: By implication, the first tanna
holds that wine is not included?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר יַיִן לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'אַף הַיָּיִן' in רבי שמעון שזורי's opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Also wine' implies the others leave wine out, and that is hard to accept.

steps.title: Reword it: רבי שמעון שזורי says wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording. רבי שמעון שזורי simply says 'wine,' not 'wine too.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: רבי שמעון שזורי says: wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing how we read רבי שמעון שזורי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the word 'too' is removed, רבי שמעון שזורי is no longer adding wine to a list. He is naming wine as the liquid in this group instead of oil and honey. That way nothing implies that the others reject wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (read the text this way)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון שזורי is not adding wine to oil and honey. In the corrected reading, his opinion is about wine instead of them.
steps.whatToRemember: By רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer, the ruling that follows רבי שמעון שזורי is about wine.

phrases.english: Say instead:
Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says: Wine.
phrases.notes: He means wine, but not oil and honey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: יָיִן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי שמעון שזורי was adding wine to the others' list.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון שזורי names wine in place of oil and honey.

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי's story: טבל mixed into חולין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי שמעון שזורי's טבל got mixed with חולין. רבי טרפון told him to buy produce from the market and separate מעשר from it for the mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון שזורי said: Once my טבל got mixed with חולין. I came and asked רבי טרפון, and he told me: Go take produce from the market and separate מעשר from it on behalf of the mixture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רבי שמעון שזורי, a story about a problem he had with mixed produce. Steps 8–13 explain the reasoning behind רבי טרפון's advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל is produce that has not yet been tithed, so it cannot be eaten until מעשר is taken. Once it was mixed with already-tithed חולין, it was unclear how to tithe it. רבי טרפון's solution was to use produce bought in the market to separate מעשר for the mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce that has not been tithed yet and is forbidden to eat
Ordinary produce (here, produce that was already tithed)
Got mixed
Market
Separate מעשר on its behalf

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri said:
Once, there became mixed for me
untithed produce with non-sacred produce,
and I came and asked Rabbi Tarfon,
and he said to me:
Go, take for yourself from the market
and separate tithes on its behalf.
phrases.notes: 'On its behalf' means for the mixture that has the טבל in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי: פַּעַם אַחַת נִתְעָרֵב לִי טֶבֶל בְּחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: another teaching of רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When טבל is mixed with חולין, one takes produce from the market and separates מעשר from it for the mixture.

steps.title: Why market produce works: exempt for exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון holds that by Torah law the טבל is nullified in the majority, and that most עמי הארץ tithe. So separating from market produce counts as separating from exempt produce for exempt produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that by Torah law the טבל is cancelled out in the majority, and that most עמי הארץ do tithe. So taking from market produce is like separating from exempt produce for exempt produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the logic behind רבי טרפון's advice to buy produce from the market.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the small amount of טבל is nullified in the larger amount of tithed חולין, so it is exempt. Only the רבנן still require tithing it. Market produce from an עם הארץ is also exempt by Torah law, since most of them tithe, yet the רבנן still require tithing it. Both sides are in the same status, so the separation works.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (as opposed to a rule of the רבנן)
Nullified in the majority. A small amount mixed into a larger amount loses its own status.
Unlearned people who are not trusted to have tithed their produce
One who separates תרומה or מעשר
Exempt (here: not obligated in tithes by Torah law)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'exempt' means nothing needs to be done. Both the mixture and the market produce still need tithing because the רבנן require it. 'Exempt' here only means exempt by Torah law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key principle for the rest of the סוגיא. You may only separate from produce in the same Torah-level status as the produce you are fixing.

phrases.english: He holds that by Torah law it is nullified in the majority,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי טרפון, and 'it' is the small amount of טבל that got mixed into the חולין in Step 7.

phrases.english: and most עמי הארץ do tithe,
and so he is like one who separates
from exempt produce for exempt produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי טרפון's instruction in the ברייתא from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Market produce is exempt by Torah law, since most עמי הארץ tithe, and so is the nullified טבל. So this is separating from exempt produce for exempt produce.

steps.title: Why not tell him to take from a gentile?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי טרפון didn't simply tell him to take produce from a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him tell him: 'Go take from a gentile!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי טרפון's choice. A גוי's produce seems like an even simpler option, so why send him to the market?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גוי's produce is also exempt by Torah law, it would match the mixture's status just as well. The question is why רבי טרפון chose the market over this option. This step sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But let him say to him.' This suggests a different instruction that would seem better.
A non-Jew

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
"Go take from the gentile"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: לֵךְ קַח מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice of market produce explained in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's choice of market produce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גוי's produce seems like an equally good, or even more obvious, source of produce that is exempt by Torah law.

steps.title: A gentile's ownership does not remove the land's obligation
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון holds that a גוי's ownership of land in ארץ ישראל does not cancel the obligation of מעשר. So a גוי's produce is obligated by Torah law and cannot be used for exempt produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that a gentile's ownership in ארץ ישראל does not remove the land from the obligation of מעשר. So it would be separating from obligated produce for exempt produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a גוי's produce would not work, because רבי טרפון holds it is still obligated by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גוי's ownership does not remove the land's holiness, his produce stays obligated in מעשר by Torah law. The mixture, though, is exempt by Torah law. Separating from obligated produce for exempt produce does not work, so the market was the right choice.

keyTerms.meaning: A גוי's ownership of land does not take effect to change its status
To cancel or remove (here: the land's obligation)
Obligated (here: obligated in tithes by Torah law)

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, רבי טרפון holds two things: most עמי הארץ tithe, and a גוי's ownership does not cancel מעשר. That is why the market works and the גוי does not.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: אֵין קִנְיָן לְגוֹי בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: He holds: a gentile has no ownership in ארץ ישראל
that would remove it from the obligation of מעשר,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ מִן הַחִיּוּב עַל הַפְּטוּר.
phrases.english: and so it would be from obligated produce for exempt produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: אֵין קִנְיָן לְגוֹי בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a legal position of רבי טרפון that rules out the suggested option
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי's produce would be exempt by Torah law and would work just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי's produce is obligated by Torah law, so it cannot be used for the exempt mixture.

steps.title: Another version: he did say to take from a gentile
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי טרפון actually told him to take from a גוי. In this version he holds that a גוי's ownership does cancel מעשר, so it is exempt for exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he told him: 'Go take from a gentile,' because he holds that a gentile's ownership in ארץ ישראל does remove the obligation of מעשר. So it is from exempt produce for exempt produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the story. In this version, רבי טרפון's advice was to take from a גוי, not from the market.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, a גוי's ownership cancels the Torah obligation of מעשר. So his produce is exempt by Torah law, just like the nullified mixture. The same principle of exempt for exempt still holds; only the source of the produce changes.

keyTerms.meaning: A גוי's ownership does take effect and removes the land's obligation

phrases.english: There are those who say:
he said to him: "Go take from the gentile,"

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר יֵשׁ קִנְיָן לְגוֹי בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: he holds a gentile has ownership in ארץ ישראל
that removes it from the obligation of מעשר,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ מִן הַפְּטוּר עַל הַפְּטוּר.
phrases.english: and so it is from exempt produce for exempt produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֵךְ קַח מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a different version of רבי טרפון's instruction from the one explained in Steps 8–10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, a גוי's produce is exempt by Torah law, so he may separate from it for the exempt mixture.

steps.title: Why not tell him to take from the market?
steps.stepSummary: In this second version, the גמרא asks why רבי טרפון didn't send him to the market instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him tell him: 'Take from the market!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version. Why choose a גוי over the simpler option of market produce?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If most עמי הארץ tithe, market produce would also be exempt by Torah law and would work. So why did he choose the גוי? This step sets up the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The market, where people buy produce from עמי הארץ

phrases.english: But let him say to him: "Take from the market"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version in Step 11, the mirror image of the challenge in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version's choice of a גוי's produce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Market produce would seem to be an equally valid source of produce that is exempt by Torah law.

steps.title: Most עמי הארץ do not tithe
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי טרפון holds that most עמי הארץ do not tithe. So market produce is obligated by Torah law and cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that most עמי הארץ do not tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in this version, market produce would not work, because most עמי הארץ do not tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If most עמי הארץ do not tithe, market produce is obligated by Torah law. Using it for the exempt mixture would be separating from obligated produce for exempt produce. So the only option is a גוי's produce.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not separate מעשר

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions are mirror images. In the first, most עמי הארץ tithe and a גוי's ownership does not cancel מעשר, so he goes to the market. In the second, most עמי הארץ do not tithe and a גוי's ownership does cancel מעשר, so he goes to a גוי. Both follow the same rule: exempt for exempt.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: אֵין רוֹב עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מְעַשְּׂרִין.
phrases.english: He holds: most עמי הארץ do not tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: אֵין רוֹב עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מְעַשְּׂרִין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a factual and legal position of רבי טרפון that rules out the suggested option
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Market produce would be exempt by Torah law and could be used.
steps.terutzMaskana: Most עמי הארץ do not tithe, so market produce is obligated by Torah law and cannot be used for the exempt mixture.

steps.title: Does the rule about רבי שמעון שזורי include the mixed טבל case?
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר בר שלמיא asks רב פפא whether רבי חנינא's rule, that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי everywhere, also applies to the case of טבל mixed with חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר בר שלמיא sent a question to רב פפא. רבי חנינא said that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי. He also said that anywhere רבי שמעון שזורי taught something, the הלכה follows him. Does that include even the case where his טבל got mixed up with חולין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: someone asks how far a general rule about רבי שמעון שזורי reaches. It is checking whether the rule includes the story we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא gave a wide rule: wherever רבי שמעון שזורי taught, the הלכה follows him. The doubt is whether that rule covers only his rulings in the משנה, or also a teaching from a ברייתא like the story of his טבל mixed with חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of ...
And not only that, but even more
Any place where he taught

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya sent to Rav Pappa:
That which Ravin bar Chinnana said
that Ulla said that Rabbi Chanina said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri,
and not only that, but

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי
phrases.english: any place where Rabbi Shimon Shezuri taught
the halacha follows him,
even in the case where his untithed produce got mixed with tithed produce?
phrases.notes: This is the story we just learned, where רבי שמעון שזורי's own produce got mixed up and he asked רבי טרפון what to do.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from analyzing רבי טרפון's advice to asking whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in this case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי חנינא's general rule covers the case of טבל mixed with חולין.

steps.title: רב פפא answers yes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that yes, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי even in the case of טבל mixed with חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question with one word: yes. The rule covers this case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי שמעון שזורי here means following the ruling he reported in his story: the mixed טבל can be fixed by separating מעשר from other produce that is also exempt by Torah law, as רבי טרפון told him. The גמרא gave two versions of where that produce comes from: the market or a גוי. רב פפא does not limit רבי חנינא's wide rule to rulings found in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי even in the mixed טבל case.

steps.title: Wasn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports in the name of מר זוטרא that רבי חנינא מסורא challenged the question: it is obvious!
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: מר זוטרא told me that רבי חנינא מסורא found this difficult. It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: A later sage challenges the whole question and answer. He asks why anyone needed to ask, since the answer seems plain. This sets up an explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא had already said 'any place where רבי שמעון שזורי taught, the הלכה follows him.' The words 'any place' seem to include this case automatically. So asking about it, and answering 'yes,' seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a difficulty with it
It is obvious! Why would this need to be said?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא מסורא is not the same person as רבי חנינא who made the rule. He is a different sage, from the town of סורא, who is questioning the discussion.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲמַר לִי מָר זוּטְרָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Mar Zutra said to me:
Rabbi Chanina of Sura raised a difficulty with it:
It is obvious!
phrases.notes: He means: 'any place' already includes this case, so why ask?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָשֵׁי בַּהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the question and answer of steps 14-15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question of רב יימר בר שלמיא and רב פפא's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'any place' clearly includes every ruling of רבי שמעון שזורי. So asking about this specific case seems unnecessary.
